crops.name: Rice
crops.description: Rice requires high moisture, warm temperatures, and standing water during most of its growing period.

temperature.low: Temperature is below the ideal range. Crop growth may slow down.
temperature.ideal: Temperature is ideal for healthy rice growth.
temperature.high: High temperature detected. Irrigate during evening hours.

humidity.low: Humidity is lower than recommended. Increase irrigation if needed.
humidity.high: High humidity may increase fungal disease risk.

soilMoisture.critical: Soil is extremely dry. Irrigate immediately.
soilMoisture.low: Soil moisture is low. Moderate irrigation recommended.
soilMoisture.high: Soil is over-watered. Stop irrigation temporarily.

airQuality.good: Air quality is suitable for crop growth.
airQuality.poor: Poor air quality may reduce plant health.

diseaseRisk.name: Leaf Blast
diseaseRisk.risk: High humidity may promote fungal infection.

diseaseRisk.name: Heat Stress
diseaseRisk.risk: Very high temperature can reduce crop yield.

tips: Maintain standing water during vegetative stage.

aiPrompt.healthy: Current environmental conditions are favorable for rice cultivation.
aiPrompt.warning: One or more environmental parameters require attention.
aiPrompt.critical: Immediate corrective action is recommended to avoid crop stress.

crops.name: Wheat
crops.description: Wheat grows best in cool, dry weather during its early growth and warm, sunny weather during ripening.

fertilizer.nitrogen: Apply half at crown root initiation and half at tillering
fertilizer.phosphorus: Apply full dose as basal application during sowing
fertilizer.potassium: Apply along with phosphorus during basal application

temperature.low: Temperature is colder than ideal. Frost protection may be needed during early stages.
temperature.ideal: Temperature is optimal for grain filling and maturation.
temperature.high: High temperature during terminal growth stage may cause forced maturity.

humidity.low: Low humidity is acceptable, but ensure adequate soil moisture during tillering.
humidity.high: High humidity increases vulnerability to rust and powdery mildew.

soilMoisture.critical: Severe moisture stress detected. Irrigate immediately at critical stages.
soilMoisture.low: Soil moisture is low. Schedule irrigation soon.
soilMoisture.high: Excess moisture detected. Prevent waterlogging to protect roots.

airQuality.good: Air quality is suitable for crop growth.
airQuality.poor: High pollution levels may impair photosynthetic activity.

diseaseRisk.name: Powdery Mildew
diseaseRisk.risk: Cool, humid conditions promote powdery mildew.

diseaseRisk.name: Loose Smut
diseaseRisk.risk: Use certified treated seeds to reduce infection.

tips: Ensure first irrigation at Crown Root Initiation stage (20-25 days after sowing).
Avoid heavy irrigation during strong winds to prevent lodging.
Maintain adequate spacing for optimal sunlight penetration.

aiPrompt.healthy: Environmental conditions are optimal for wheat growth and grain maturation.
aiPrompt.warning: Certain environmental metrics deviate from the target range for wheat.
aiPrompt.critical: Critical environmental conditions detected. Action required to safeguard wheat yield.

crops.name: Maize
crops.description: Maize thrives in well-drained fertile soils with plenty of sunshine and warm growing temperatures.

fertilizer.nitrogen: Split into 3 doses: sowing, knee-high stage, and tasseling
fertilizer.phosphorus: Apply full dose as basal application during land preparation
fertilizer.potassium: Apply half as basal and half during knee-high stage

temperature.low: Low temperatures may delay germination and early vegetative growth.
temperature.ideal: Temperature is well-suited for photosynthetic performance.
temperature.high: Excessive heat during pollination can reduce grain set and cob size.

humidity.low: Dry air may accelerate evapotranspiration. Maintain root zone moisture.
humidity.high: High humidity combined with warm weather increases leaf blight risks.

soilMoisture.critical: Critical moisture depletion. Irrigate immediately to protect tasseling stage.
soilMoisture.low: Soil moisture is below optimal. Irrigation recommended within 48 hours.
soilMoisture.good: Soil moisture is ideal for crop development.
soilMoisture.high: Over-saturated soil detected. Maize is highly sensitive to waterlogging.

airQuality.good: Air quality is good for health and growth.
airQuality.poor: Elevated atmospheric pollutants may cause mild leaf necrosis.

diseaseRisk.name: Maydis Leaf Blight
diseaseRisk.risk: Fungal disease that spreads rapidly under humid conditions.

diseaseRisk.name: Turcicum Leaf Blight
diseaseRisk.risk: Can significantly reduce photosynthesis and grain yield.

diseaseRisk.name: Stalk Rot
diseaseRisk.risk: Weakens plant stems and increases lodging risk.

tips: Avoid water stagnation as maize roots are highly susceptible to oxygen deficiency.
Critical water requirements occur during tasseling and silking stages.
Ensure adequate nitrogen top-dressing at knee-high stage.

aiPrompt.healthy: Maize microclimate and soil moisture levels are balanced.
aiPrompt.warning: Elevated stress detected in current weather or soil metrics.
aiPrompt.critical: Immediate field management required to prevent yield loss in maize crop.

crops.name: Potato
crops.description: Potato requires cool weather, well-drained loose soil, and consistent moisture for tuber initiation and enlargement.

fertilizer.nitrogen: Apply half as basal and half during earthing-up stage
fertilizer.phosphorus: Apply full dose as basal application in furrow
fertilizer.potassium: Apply full dose as basal to enhance tuber development and quality

temperature.low: Temperatures below 10°C slow tuber growth and increase frost risk.
temperature.high: Night temperatures above 20°C hinder tuber enlargement.

humidity.low: Low air humidity accelerates leaf water loss. Maintain uniform irrigation.
humidity.ideal: Humidity range is within favorable limits.
humidity.high: High humidity coupled with cool weather creates favorable conditions for late blight.

soilMoisture.critical: Severe water deficiency. Irrigate promptly to prevent tuber cracking.
soilMoisture.low: Moisture level is low. Light sprinkler or furrow irrigation recommended.
soilMoisture.good: Soil moisture is optimal for vegetative and tuber stages.
soilMoisture.high: Excess moisture promotes tuber rot and poor aeration. Reduce irrigation.

airQuality.good: Air quality is suitable for normal crop physiology.
airQuality.poor: Poor air quality can stunt canopy accumulation.

diseaseRisk.name: Late Blight
diseaseRisk.risk: Highly destructive fungal disease; monitor humidity closely.

diseaseRisk.name: Early Blight
diseaseRisk.risk: Can reduce foliage health and tuber yield.

diseaseRisk.name: Common Scab
diseaseRisk.risk: Maintain adequate soil moisture to reduce infection.

tips: Perform earthing-up 30 days after planting to prevent tuber greening.
Maintain consistent moisture; fluctuating dry and wet cycles cause knobby tubers.
Stop irrigation 10-15 days prior to harvesting to harden potato skin.

aiPrompt.healthy: Growing conditions are optimal for potato vegetative growth and tuber development.
aiPrompt.warning: Sub-optimal conditions observed; field monitoring recommended.
aiPrompt.critical: Critical environmental risk detected. Take immediate preventive measures.

crops.name: Tomato
crops.description: Tomato is a warm-season crop requiring abundant sunshine, moderate humidity, and well-drained nutrient-rich soil.

fertilizer.nitrogen: Apply in 3 split doses: basal, 30 days after transplanting, and fruit set
fertilizer.phosphorus: Apply complete dose at soil preparation
fertilizer.potassium: Apply split doses along with nitrogen to support continuous fruiting

temperature.low: Cool temperatures below 15°C reduce pollen viability and fruit set.
temperature.ideal: Temperature is ideal for flowering, fruiting, and color development.
temperature.high: Temperatures above 32°C lead to flower drop and poor fruit development.

humidity.low: Very dry conditions increase risk of blossom end rot if watering is irregular.
humidity.ideal: Humidity level supports optimal canopy growth.
humidity.high: High relative humidity promotes fungal pathogens like early blight and wilt.

soilMoisture.critical: Severe moisture stress. Water immediately to avoid blossom drop and wilt.
soilMoisture.low: Soil moisture is declining. Apply drip irrigation.
soilMoisture.good: Moisture levels are optimal for fruit development.
soilMoisture.high: Excess moisture causes root suffocation and fruit cracking.

airQuality.good: Air quality is good for plant respiration.
airQuality.poor: High pollution levels can damage delicate leaf tissues.

diseaseRisk.name: Tomato Leaf Curl Virus
diseaseRisk.risk: Monitor vectors and remove infected plants promptly.

diseaseRisk.name: Early Blight
diseaseRisk.risk: Maintain airflow and apply preventive fungicides if necessary.

diseaseRisk.name: Bacterial Wilt
diseaseRisk.risk: Improve drainage and rotate crops to reduce disease pressure.

tips: Use drip irrigation to keep foliage dry and prevent fungal leaf spot diseases.
Maintain consistent moisture levels to prevent Blossom End Rot.
Provide staking or trellising for indeterminate varieties to keep fruit off the ground.

aiPrompt.healthy: Environmental variables are optimal for healthy tomato growth and fruit production.
aiPrompt.warning: Environmental stress factors detected; review crop health parameters.
aiPrompt.critical: Severe environmental imbalance. Prompt intervention is required to avoid crop damage.
